trigger: a fresh Postgres deployment on a host whose data or config directory still holds enrollment-tokens.cfg or pending-agents.cfg from an unrelated earlier install (package removed but not purged, or only the DB volume dropped): the first-boot importer (server.cpp:5250, enrollment_cfg_import.cpp) activates them with no provenance or age check
summary: STILL OPEN; requires an OWNER edit of the contract text at docs/user-manual/upgrading.md:601 (not made). Mitigated by disclosure in upgrading.md:5 (banner), CHANGELOG.md:440 and disaster-recovery.md:20-25, but upgrading.md:601 still says 'no data imported from earlier builds' and its checklist has no leftover-.cfg item, and README.md:193 does not mention it. security-guardian re-derives MEDIUM/SHOULD (disclosure in three places; no longer concealed) but a de-escalation needs an adjudicator who is not the author, so severity_mapped is NOT lowered here. Verified in code: server.cpp:5236-5256 run_legacy_enrollment_import over data_dir and the auth-config directory; enrollment_cfg_import.cpp:140-210 keeps hash, max_uses, use_count, expires, revoked; a fresh database has no fingerprint marker to refuse a stale file. Text the owner must add to the Deployment contract paragraph: 'The server imports any enrollment-tokens.cfg and pending-agents.cfg found in --data-dir or the directory of the auth config at first boot (an empty database has no marker to refuse them), without checking where they came from. Imported tokens (with the use_count and revoked state from the file) and approved pending agents are live credentials. Before the first boot of a fresh deployment, confirm both files, and their .imported renames, are absent from both directories.' and qualify 'no data imported' to 'no database or backup data imported'.
classification_rationale: contract checklist omits a live credential-import path
